bib.title: GloVe: Global Vectors for Word Representation

question: What model properties make vector arithmetic capture word regularities, and can a model trained on global co-occurrence counts match or beat local context-window methods?
hypothesis: Ratios of co-occurrence probabilities, not raw probabilities, are the right starting point for word vector learning, so a global log-bilinear weighted least squares model should combine count-based efficiency with prediction-based linear substructure.
contributions: Derivation of a global log-bilinear regression objective from co-occurrence probability ratios
A weighted least squares model (GloVe) trained only on nonzero entries of the word-word co-occurrence matrix
Analogy, similarity and NER results above baselines; released code and vectors

method.summary: Builds a word-word co-occurrence matrix X from a tokenised, lowercased corpus (distance-weighted 1/d), then fits word and context vectors by weighted least squares on log X_ij with AdaGrad over nonzero entries. The final vector is W + W~. Evaluated on word analogy, five similarity sets and CoNLL-2003 NER.

models.name: GloVe
models.architecture: log-bilinear weighted least squares on co-occurrence; two vector sets W and W~ plus biases
models.hidden: 50 (NER), 100, 300 (analogy and similarity); dimensions varied 0-600 in Fig 2
models.context: 10 words left and 10 right unless noted

models.name: word2vec SG and CBOW (SG dagger, CBOW dagger)
SVD, SVD-S, SVD-L
models.architecture: SVD of truncated X (top 10,000 columns); of X, sqrt(X), log(1+X)

models.name: HPCA, ivLBL, vLBL, HSMN, CW, CBOW*

other.note: HPCA, HSMN, CW use public vectors; ivLBL/vLBL numbers from Mnih et al. 2013; SG/CBOW numbers from Mikolov et al. 2013a,b

training.objective: J = sum_ij f(X_ij)(w_i^T w~_j + b_i + b~_j - log X_ij)^2, f(x)=(x/xmax)^alpha if x<xmax else 1
training.optimizer: AdaGrad, stochastic sampling of nonzero elements of X
training.epochs: 50 iterations for vectors under 300 dims, 100 otherwise
training.wall_clock: about 85 minutes to build X (6B tokens, single thread); 14 minutes per iteration (300d, 32 cores)

other.init: random (W and W~ differ only by random init when X symmetric)

inference.samples: single run per configuration; no seeds or variance reported

parameters.analogy: answer d maximising cosine similarity to w_b - w_a + w_c; exact match only
parameters.similarity: normalise each feature across vocabulary then cosine; Spearman correlation with human judgments
parameters.NER: CRF (CRFjoin of Wang and Manning 2013), 50d vectors of a five-word context as continuous features, L-BFGS stopping after 25 iterations without dev improvement

limits: No variance, seeds or significance tests; single runs.
word2vec comparison holds unspecified parameters at defaults, admitted as a simplification to relax in a more thorough analysis.
Choice alpha=3/4 has only empirical motivation.
Semantic analogy accuracy drops on Gigaword vs Wikipedia; authors attribute it to the city/country-heavy analogy set, untested.
840B-token run reported without numbers and not comparable (cased).
Static word-level vectors, one vector per word, no OOV or subword handling; 2014 baselines only; analogy evaluation has since been criticised (not in paper).

terms.definition: A context window that extends to the left and right of a target word will be called symmetric, and one which extends only to the left will be called asymmetric.
Global Vectors, because the global corpus statistics are captured directly by the model.
